'''Athanassios Giannis''' (born 22 January 1954) is a Greek [[chemist]] and [[Medical doctor|physician]]. He is a professor emeritus at [[Leipzig University]], where he held a professorship in [[organic chemistry]] and natural products chemistry.<ref name="GiannisCV">{{cite web
|title=Curriculum vitae – Prof. Athanassios Giannis
|url=https://home.uni-leipzig.de/mct/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/GiannisCV-BBZ-2021.pdf

|publisher=Leipzig University (Molecular Cell Therapy / BBZ)
|format=PDF
|access-date=2025-12-13
}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Giannis was born in [[Drama]], [[Greece]]. He studied chemistry at the [[University of Bonn]] (1972–1980) and medicine at the University of Bonn (1978–1988).<ref name="GiannisCV"/> He completed his diploma thesis in 1980 with [[Manfred T. Reetz]] and earned a PhD (Dr. rer. nat.) in 1986 under Konrad Sandhoff. He obtained his habilitation (venia legendi) in organic chemistry and biochemistry at the University of Bonn in 1992.<ref name="GiannisCV"/>

In a 2019 autobiographical account, Giannis wrote that he grew up under poor conditions in a small mountain village in northern Greece and moved to Bonn after school to study, stating that “all my belongings fit into a plastic bag”.<ref name="Synlett2019">{{cite journal
|last=Giannis
|first=Athanassios
|title=On Artemisinin, Cyclopamine, D-Isocitric Acid, Hyperforin, Epigenetics, Sialic Acid, and More
|journal=Synlett
|year=2019
|volume=30
|issue=12
|pages=1401–1418
|doi=10.1055/s-0037-1611775
}}</ref>

== Academic career ==
From 1992 to 1997, Giannis was associate professor of organic chemistry at the University of Bonn. From 1997 to 2002, he was professor of organic chemistry at the [[University of Karlsruhe]] (TH). In 2002, he moved to Leipzig University as full professor of organic chemistry and chemistry of natural products, and he later became professor emeritus.<ref name="GiannisCV"/>

Since 2020, he has also been listed as visiting professor at [[Leipzig University]]'s Center for Biotechnology and Biomedicine (BBZ) and at the [[Leibniz Institute of Plant Biochemistry]] (IPB) in [[Halle (Saale)|Halle]], [[Germany]].<ref name="GiannisCV"/>

== Research ==
Giannis works in biologically and medicinally oriented organic chemistry, combining synthetic methodology and natural product synthesis with medicinal-chemistry and chemical-biology questions. Research topics associated with his work include epigenetics; inhibitors of histone-modifying enzymes; immunomodulatory drugs and cereblon ligands; PROTAC-related concepts; nucleoside analogues; and the synthesis of bioactive natural products.<ref name="GiannisCV"/>

In 2009, Giannis and co-authors reported a biomimetic, diastereoselective synthesis of cyclopamine in ''Angewandte Chemie International Edition'', which later reviews describe as the first synthesis of cyclopamine (via a semisynthetic approach).<ref name="Cyclopamine2009">{{cite journal
|title=Synthesis of cyclopamine using a biomimetic and diastereoselective approach
|journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition
|year=2009
|doi=10.1002/anie.200902520
|pmid=19591183
}}</ref><ref name="BJOC2025">{{cite journal
|last1=Mögel
|first1=Morwenna
|last2=Berger
|first2=David
|last3=Heretsch
|first3=Philipp
|title=Recent advancements in the synthesis of ''Veratrum'' alkaloids
|journal=Beilstein Journal of Organic Chemistry
|volume=21
|pages=2657–2693
|doi=10.3762/bjoc.21.206
|date=2025-12-10
|pmc=12706376
}}</ref> The same review describes the first total synthesis of cyclopamine as being reported in 2023 by another group.<ref name="BJOC2025"/>

In 2018, Giannis co-authored a study reporting the total synthesis and biological investigation of (−)-artemisinin and its natural antipode (+)-artemisinin, concluding that antimalarial activity is not stereospecific.<ref name="Artemisinin2018">{{cite journal
|title=The antimalarial activity of artemisinin is not stereospecific
|journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition
|year=2018
|doi=10.1002/anie.201802015
|pmid=29723442
}}</ref>

== Health system and humanitarian engagement ==
In a 2015 interview with ''Telepolis'' during the Greek debt crisis, Giannis discussed the humanitarian situation in Greece, including problems in healthcare provision, and addressed the implications for vulnerable groups, including refugees.<ref name="Telepolis2015">{{cite web
|title=Die griechische Katastrophe
|url=https://www.telepolis.de/article/Die-griechische-Katastrophe-3374524.html?seite=all

|website=Telepolis
|date=2015-07-28
|language=de
|access-date=2025-12-13
}}</ref>

Giannis has also been associated with the humanitarian initiative ''Medikamenten-Nothilfe für Griechenland'' (Medication emergency aid for Greece). In a 2020 interview, he described the initiative as having been established in 2015 to support access to medicines and medical supplies and stated that, during the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], support shifted toward medical equipment for an ambulance service providing examinations and preventive care in remote regions of Greece, including support for children and refugees.<ref name="HalleSpektrum2020">{{cite web
|title=Corona-Pandemie: Warten auf Medikamente und Impfstoffe – wie ist der Stand der Dinge?
|url=https://hallespektrum.de/aktuelles/corona-pandemie-warten-auf-medikamente-und-impfstoffe-wie-ist-der-stand-der-dinge/374534/

|website=HalleSpektrum
|date=2020-05-04
|language=de
|access-date=2025-12-13
}}</ref> A 2015 newspaper report referred to the initiative as collaborating with Giannis and partners in Leipzig and Patras.<ref name="Leinetal2015">{{cite web
|title=Medikamente für Griechenland
|url=https://www.leinetal24.de/lokales/bockenem/medikamente-griechenland-5511196.html

|website=leinetal24.de
|date=2015-09-08
|language=de
|access-date=2025-12-13
}}</ref>
